subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls fail closed on legacy ownerless session rows, accepting that existing plugin flows may lose patch access until an operator manages those rows through a non-plugin client?
rationale: No safe plugin owner can be inferred for an ownerless persisted row, so preserving access weakens cross-plugin isolation while rejecting access creates an intentional upgrade break that only maintainers can authorize.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document operator recovery, and require deployed proof before merge.

options.title: Design an adoption path
options.body: Pause the PR until a narrow, explicitly authorized migration or ownership-adoption mechanism is specified and tested.

options.title: Preserve legacy access
options.body: Allow plugin runtimes to continue patching ownerless rows, retaining compatibility at the cost of an incomplete ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugin runtimes, document operator recovery, and require deployed proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows repeated ownership of gateway session migration, reset, and shared helper boundaries, which are central to this compatibility and security decision.
